title: Lior and the Provision
premise: Riverboat captain Isandro Vane has spent years running cargo and dodging debts along the Verrow River, keeping his head down and his past buried. When a dying prospector named Lior trades him a hand-drawn map to the river's forbidden source in exchange for a promise to deliver it somewhere safe, Isandro inherits a treasure he never wanted and a crew of strays who slowly become the family he refused to admit he needed. Pursued by the Provision Company, which will kill to keep the source's power sealed, Isandro must choose between surrendering the map to protect his people or racing upstream through the glacier's brief calving window. In the end, Isandro reaches the source, discovers it is not gold but a living spring of rare mineral wealth that corrupts all who claim it, and chooses to destroy the map and flood the approach—sacrificing his boat, his debt, and any claim to fortune—to keep his found family free.
about_author: Casper Eastwick is the pen name of a former barge mechanic who spent six seasons working inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about rivers, rust, and the people who choose each other over profit.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Isandro Vane pilots his aging riverboat, the Kestrel, down the lower Verrow, hounded by a Provision Company collector demanding payment on his father's debt. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: weary resignation—the quiet cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Landing
chapters.summary: At a muddy trading post, Isandro finds a prospector named Lior collapsed on his dock, feverish and half-starved. Against his better judgment, he takes the old man aboard. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion cracking his practiced indifference.

chapters.title: What the Dying Trade
chapters.summary: Lior offers Isandro a grease-stained map to the river's forbidden source in exchange for one promise: carry it upstream before calving season opens the route. Isandro refuses, then watches Lior worsen. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the trap of being needed.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Lior dies at dawn with Isandro's hand in his, whispering that the map is 'a debt owed to everyone.' Isandro buries him on the bank and pockets the map he swore not to take. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: guilt binding him to a promise made too late.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: At Greyford Landing, Isandro takes on three drifters: Sefa, a disgraced cartographer; Bram, a deserter with strong hands; and Nell, an orphan girl stowing away among cargo crates. POV: rotating among the three newcomers. Emotional beat: wary strangers circling, each hiding something.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Provision Company agents board the Kestrel searching for Lior's effects. Isandro lies smoothly, but agent Corvus Hale marks the boat for surveillance. POV: Isandro, with a tense exchange with Hale. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Nell Opens the Map
chapters.summary: Nell discovers the hidden map and, fascinated, spreads it across the deck; Sefa recognizes the survey style and confirms it is genuine—and valuable. The crew now knows what Isandro carries. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: wonder and the first spark of shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Vote Below Decks
chapters.summary: Isandro confesses the promise he made Lior. Sefa argues the source could restore her name; Bram wants nothing to do with it; Nell pleads to go. They vote to run the river upstream. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: a found family forming around a dangerous choice.

chapters.title: Rapids at Thornmouth
chapters.summary: The Kestrel threads the Thornmouth rapids as Hale's gunboat shadows them. A near-capsize costs them half their cargo and cements the crew's trust in Isandro's skill. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into loyalty.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Hale intercepts them at a fueling station and offers to erase Isandro's debt in exchange for the map. Isandro almost takes it—until he sees how casually Hale discusses killing witnesses. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: temptation met with revulsion.

chapters.title: Sefa's Country
chapters.summary: Entering unmapped territory, Sefa charts by starlight and instinct, rediscovering confidence she thought lost. She and Isandro share a quiet night watch and the first honest conversation either has had in years. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: love kindling against both their better judgments.

chapters.title: The Frozen Gate
chapters.summary: They reach the glacier's mouth weeks early; the passage is still sealed. Forced to wait, the crew grows restless, and Bram confesses why he deserted—a massacre he was ordered to join. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: shame laid down like a heavy pack.

chapters.title: Nell's Discovery
chapters.summary: Exploring the ice caves while they wait, Nell finds Lior's old camp and journals revealing the source isn't gold—it's a mineral spring the Company poisoned towns to conceal. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: innocence confronting institutional evil.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ice Line
chapters.summary: Bram, terrified of what the journals mean for his own crimes, secretly signals Hale's position. Isandro catches him at the signal mirror; the family fractures overnight. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deeper because it came from kin.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: The glacier groans and splits—the route opens for a matter of days. With Hale's gunboat closing in, Isandro must decide whether to bring the broken Bram or leave him. He brings him. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: forgiveness chosen before it is felt.

chapters.title: The White Reach
chapters.summary: A brutal push through the calving channel: falling ice, freezing spray, the Kestrel taking fatal damage. Sefa navigates by memory and nerve as the boat begins to die beneath them. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: love expressed as competence under fire.

chapters.title: Corvus Hale
chapters.summary: Hale corners them in a narrow bend; a firefight erupts on the ice. Bram redeems himself by disabling the gunboat's rudder at terrible personal cost, and Hale retreats vowing to return with a fleet. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with blood.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: On foot, the survivors reach the spring: luminous, beautiful, and unmistakably corrupting—Lior's final journal pages describe men it drove mad with wanting. Isandro holds the map over the water and understands his true promise. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: awe curdling into clarity.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Sefa, tempted by the fame of charting the source, argues to record its location; Isandro argues to destroy it. Their love is tested against duty to truth versus duty to each other. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: the hardest argument two loving people can have.

chapters.title: The Flooded Approach
chapters.summary: Isandro collapses the ice shelf sealing the spring's outflow, drowning the approach route forever and destroying the map in the torrent. The Kestrel, already lost, goes down with it. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: grief and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: The four walk out together over weeks, poorer than they started and richer than they imagined. Hale's fleet arrives to find only a sealed valley. Isandro's debt dies with the Company's leverage. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: quiet triumph of the unremarkable and unbroken.

chapters.title: The Kestrel's Wake
chapters.summary: One year later, the four run a small ferry on a different river under new names. Nell asks if they'll ever tell anyone about the source. Isandro answers: 'We already did—we told each other.' POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: home found not in a place but in the people beside you.
